answer.decision: Adopt the managed search service behind an internal abstraction and portable index pipeline.
answer.action: Use the managed service for the four-month launch. Define a vendor-neutral canonical search document, isolate vendor-specific indexing and query code behind an internal interface, automate complete exports and index rebuilds, and validate a migration runbook before production scale-up.
reasons: The managed service supports faceting, typo tolerance, and near-real-time indexing, directly meeting the launch requirements.

Building immediately is incompatible with staffing and schedule constraints: the prior prototype consumed six engineer-weeks without delivering faceting or typo tolerance, and operating a cluster would require on-call ownership and quarterly upgrades.
Delaying for dedicated hires would miss the four-month deadline and risk forfeiting a contracted design-partner expansion.
Projected first-year cost is limited to 7 percent of the product infrastructure budget.
A canonical search document and documented bulk export API provide the foundations for a practical, testable migration path.
Search relevance is important but not a core differentiator, so immediate infrastructure ownership is not justified.
assumptions: The managed service meets applicable latency, availability, security, privacy, and data-residency requirements.
The team has sufficient capacity within four months to integrate the service, implement a focused abstraction, and establish observability.
Bulk export includes the data and metadata needed to reconstruct indexes at acceptable throughput and cost.
The abstraction targets indexing, querying, and result translation without attempting to hide every vendor-specific capability.
risks: Vendor-specific ranking semantics and advanced features may leak through the abstraction, increasing migration effort.
Costs may rise materially with traffic, index size, or query complexity.
Export and reindex throughput may make migration slower than planned.
An overly broad abstraction could delay launch, while an overly narrow one could weaken portability.
Vendor outages, policy changes, or service discontinuation could affect availability.

citations.claim: The managed service supports all required launch features and provides a documented bulk export API.
The prior prototype required six engineer-weeks and still lacked typo tolerance and faceting.
Operating the open-source cluster would require rotating primary on-call ownership and quarterly upgrade work.
A six-month delay would forgo a contracted design-partner expansion.
Projected year-one managed-service spending is 7 percent of the product infrastructure budget.
The product data model can emit a vendor-neutral canonical search document before indexing.
